mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% indicates a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 4% but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth accelerates and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals strong economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 growth and UNRATE reduction occur but SPX returns are not positive in majority of 60-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during an early-cycle expansion regime suggests increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases but SPX returns are negative in more than 35% of the next 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate increased consumer confidence and construction activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST exceeds 1200 but SPX returns are not positive in majority of 60-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) coupled with employment growth (PAYEMS) indicate robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both RSAFS and PAYEMS grow but SPX returns are not positive in majority of 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% may lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL exceeds 2% but SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) during a late-cycle expansion regime may signal impending economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 slows but SPX returns are positive in more than 35% of the next 60-day windows, the hypothesis fails.
